chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Husayn ibn Mukhtar, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I accompanied him between Mecca and Medina. A beggar came, so he ordered that he be given. Then another came, so he ordered that he be given. Then another came, so he ordered that he be given. Then the fourth came, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'May Allah satisfy you.'
Then he turned to us and said: 'Indeed, we have what we can give him, but I fear that we may become like one of the three whose supplication is not answered.'
A man whom Allah gave wealth, so he spent it in that which was not its rightful place, then he says: 'O Allah, grant me,' so it is not answered for him.
And a man who supplicates against his wife that he be freed from her, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made her matter to him.
And a man who supplicates against his neighbor, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made the way open for him to move away from his neighbor's vicinity and sell his house.

key_terms.أَنْفَقَهُ فِي غَيْرِ حَقِّهِ: He spent it in that which was not its rightful place
key_terms.يُشْبِعُكَ اللَّهُ: May Allah satisfy you (a specific supplication)

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of people whose supplication is not answered according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the principle of *hikmah* (wisdom) in charity by withholding from a fourth beggar, fearing that indiscriminate giving might lead to the supplicant becoming one of the three whose prayers are rejected. This hadith highlights that the efficacy of dua is contingent not only on sincerity but also on the recipient's conduct, specifically regarding the misuse of wealth, marital patience, and neighborly relations.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Husayn Bin Mukhtar, from Al Waleed Bin Sabeeh, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I accompanied him<sup>asws</sup> between Makkah and Al-Medina, and a beggar came over. So he<sup>asws</sup> ordered that he should be given. Then another one came over, so he<sup>asws</sup> ordered that he should be given. Then another one came over, so he<sup>asws</sup> ordered that he should be given. Then the fourth one came over, so Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Satiate you’.

Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> turned towards us and he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘But there is with us<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> what we<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> can give him, but I<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> fear lest we<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> would become like one of the three whose supplications are not Answered for them –

a man whom Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> had Given wealth, so he spent it in other that its rightful place, then says, ‘O Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>! Grace me’, so it would not be Answered for him.
And a man who I supplicating against his wife that he be freed from her, and Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has already Made her matter to him;

and a man who is supplicating against his neighbour, and Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has already Made a way for him that he can move away from his neighbour and buy his house (somewhere else)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Husayn ibn Mukhtar from al-Walid ibn Sabih who has said the following:

“Once I accompanied abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) between Makkah and Madinah and at a certain place a beggar came and he ordered his people to help. Another beggar came he ordered his people to help, another came and he ordered to help, then the fourth one came and abu ‘Abd Allah said, ‘May Allah satisfy you,’
and he turned to us saying, ‘We still can help but I feared becoming of the three kinds of people whose prayers are not heard:
a man to whom Allah has granted wealth but he spends it on a wrong cause and then asks, “O Lord, grant me wealth.” His prayer is not accepted,
a man who prays against his wife while Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has made it lawful to dissolve the marriage,
and a man who prays against his neighbor while Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has made it possible for him to move away and buy another house.’”
